(2) Semantic fidelity/ordered coverage: the chain u0 --has_key--> u1 --door_open--> u2 --at_goal--> u3 respects the environment constraints (door_open cannot precede has_key; at_goal cannot precede door_open), so the label sequences reaching u3 coincide exactly with task success. (3) Persistent/event distinctions: door_open is used as a condition (fires on the rising edge; later open/close toggling in u2 is absorbed by else); at_goal is last-step-only and lands directly in the final state; the key_lost event is irrelevant to this task and is correctly covered by the else self-loops in u0/u1 rather than rewarded or used as a regression. No regression on key_lost is required here because 'have picked up the key' is an achievement that persists, and omitting the regression also prevents drop/pickup reward farming. (4) Reward safety: rewards 0.1, 0.2, 1.0 are nonnegative, each progress transition can fire at most once (no path returns to a lower state), the maximum total is 1.3, and no self-loop carries reward. (5) Predicate-only events: all transition labels are single predicates or else, no composite events. (6) Compactness: four states is the minimal canonical chain for this milestone structure; every state has full else coverage, so the transition function is total over all proposition valuations. No defects found.
